### P-0113 v1 — Weight-security gap: SB 53 (and RAISE, Illinois) require frameworks to cover securing unreleased model weights

`change` · evidence: **Verified against inspected external sources** · decision: **accepted** (v1, 2026-10-10) · confidence: high · change-hash `982394064686`

**Linked:** P-0023, P-0075

**Applied together with:** P-0066

**Change**

- **`index.html`**

  Current:

  > BIS export controls touch the adjacent question of who can access frontier-capable hardware. No US state, no UK statute, and no other binding instrument covers weight security directly.

  Proposed:

  > California SB 53 requires the published frameworks of large frontier developers to describe how they secure unreleased model weights, and NY RAISE (2027) and Illinois (2028) copy that duty, but none sets a security level. ### P-0114 v1 — Halting gap: China can order services suspended; lab halting commitments have weakened (Anthropic, Meta)

`change` · evidence: **Verified against inspected external sources** · decision: **accepted** (v1, 2026-10-10) · confidence: medium · change-hash `5a144464f807`

**Linked:** P-0022, P-0037, P-0038, P-0039, P-0041, P-0097

**Change**

- **`index.html`**

  Current:

  > The EU AI Office can order recall (Aug 2026 onwards). The GPAI Code calls for halting at systemic-risk thresholds. Seoul commitments asked labs to commit to it. Every lab framework includes it. That\'s essentially the whole list. No US state, no other national statute, no other multilateral instrument can compel a frontier developer to pause.

  Proposed:

  > The EU AI Office can order recall (Aug 2026 onwards). China\'s GenAI Measures let regulators order a non-compliant service suspended. The GPAI Code calls for halting at systemic-risk thresholds. Seoul commitments asked labs to commit to it. Every lab framework includes halting conditions, though several have weakened: Anthropic ties its delay commitments to what competitors do, and Meta\'s v2 replaced "stop" with "develop with mitigations". That\'s essentially the whole list. No US state, and no other frontier-specific statute or multilateral instrument, can compel a frontier developer to pause.

**Why it matters:** The map's own China entry says firms have had services suspended, and Art. 21 of the GenAI Measures provides for ordering suspension — a compelled pause the gap says does not exist. 'Every lab framework includes it' no longer conveys that Anthropic's RSP v3 made delays competitor-dependent and Meta's v2 dropped 'stop'.

**Reasoning:** S-0290#6 (Art. 21: ordered to suspend the relevant services); EU recall power S-0002#20, enforcement from 2 Aug 2026 S-0280#1; GPAI Code Measure 4.2 (S-0044#3); Seoul commitment IV (S-0034#8); RSP v3.4 Appendix A (S-0006#12); Meta v2 change log (S-0107#5); OpenAI v2 Critical halt (S-0095#6).

### P-0108 v1 — Category definitions for thresholds, timing, mitigations (and evaluations) depart from METR's meaning

`question` · evidence: **Verified against inspected external sources** · decision: **withdrawn** (v1, 2026-10-10) · confidence: medium · change-hash `4f53cda18c2b`

**Question for you:** METR defines capability thresholds as 'Thresholds at which specific AI capabilities would pose severe risk and require new mitigations'; the map says 'Levels at which obligations or risks trigger', which also takes in regulatory eligibility thresholds (compute, revenue). METR's timing element is 'when and how often evaluations must be performed'; the map says 'When evaluations and obligations apply'. METR's deployment mitigations are 'access and model-level measures applied to prevent the unauthorized use of a model's dangerous capabilities'; the map says 'Refusals, monitoring, content controls'. 'Model evaluations' is not one of METR's nine. Options: (a) keep the map's broader definitions and say they are adapted (pairs with metr-taxonomy; recommended); (b) restore METR's meaning, e.g. thresh 'Capability levels that pose severe risk and require new mitigations', timing 'When and how often evaluations are performed', mit 'Access and model-level measures that prevent misuse of dangerous capabilities' — then coverage notes that rely on the broader meaning (e.g. compute-eligibility thresholds under thresh, obligation timing under timing, content moderation under mit) become stretches to mark; (c) METR wording plus a short adaptation note, e.g. thresh 'Capability levels that pose severe risk and require new mitigations (here also regulatory compute thresholds)'.

**Why it matters:** The category definitions are the page's description of what each filter means; where they diverge from METR while citing METR, readers may take the map's broader categories for METR's.

**Reasoning:** Compared each map definition with METR's component definition (metr-ce). Elicitation, weight security, halting, accountability (METR includes transparency, metr-ce#acct2) and updating match in meaning; thresholds, timing and mitigations are broadened; evaluations is the map's own addition.

**Evidence**

- **S-0204** Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies — <https://metr.org/common-elements>
  primary · retrieved 2026-10-10 · access: ok · published 2025-12-16
  Introduction, components list:
  > Capability Thresholds: Thresholds at which specific AI capabilities would pose severe risk and require new mitigations.
  _Supports:_ METR's threshold definition is capability-based
- **S-0204** Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies — <https://metr.org/common-elements>
  primary · retrieved 2026-10-10 · access: ok · published 2025-12-16
  Introduction, components list:
  > Timing and Frequency of Evaluations: Concrete timelines outlining when and how often evaluations must be performed – e.g. before deployment, during training, and after deployment.
  _Supports:_ METR's timing element is about evaluations and their frequency
- **S-0204** Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies — <https://metr.org/common-elements>
  primary · retrieved 2026-10-10 · access: ok · published 2025-12-16
  Introduction, components list:
  > Model Deployment Mitigations: Access and model-level measures applied to prevent the unauthorized use of a model’s dangerous capabilities.
  _Supports:_ METR's mitigation definition
- **S-0204** Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies — <https://metr.org/common-elements>
  primary · retrieved 2026-10-10 · access: ok · published 2025-12-16
  Introduction, components list and Table 1:
  > [Observation, not a quotation] [Observation, not a quotation] The nine components listed (and the nine rows of Table 1) are: capability thresholds, model weight security, deployment mitigations, conditions for halting deployment plans, conditions for halting development plans, capability elicitation, evaluation timing/frequency, accountability, updating policies. 'Model evaluations' is not a separate component; halting appears as two.
  _Supports:_ evaluations not a separate element

**Uncertainty:** The broadening is deliberate (gap:thresh contrasts eligibility and capability thresholds), so this is a framing choice, not a factual error.

## 3. Discovery log

### SCOPE B3: industry and multistakeholder bodies (FMF, PAI, EU codes) and summit/G7 commitments (Seoul, Delhi, Hiroshima/OECD)

No new cross-firm commitment or code since June 2026 was found. Updates to existing entries: the HAIP Reporting Framework v2.0 (28 May 2026) and publication of v2.0 reports from 31 companies (2 Oct 2026); the GPAI Code's Signatory Taskforce, chaired by the AI Office (page updated 3 Aug 2026), with the Code itself unchanged since Jul 2025; the FMF information-sharing agreement (Mar 2025, operating), absent from the map. FMF and PAI 2026 outputs are research and guidance, not mechanisms. Seoul signatories unchanged since Feb 2025; Delhi list dated 23 Feb 2026. The G7 Évian summit (15–17 Jun 2026) adopted no AI text; Macron said AI work would be finalised in ministerial formats.

### B4 labs (Layer 6): Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI — new framework versions since Jun 2026, SB 53 / RAISE / EU Code compliance frameworks, governance-body changes

No lab issued a new safety-framework version after June 2026 except xAI (FAIF effective 30 Jun 2026). But three entries described superseded versions: OpenAI's entry described the 2023 beta (v2 Apr 2025 is current); DeepMind's misdated v2/v3 (v3.1 Apr 2026 is current); Meta's missed v2's change from "stop" to "develop with mitigations". OpenAI designated GPT-6 Astra its first Critical (cyber) model on 1–3 Sep 2026 and paused some training for two weeks. Compliance documents: OpenAI's FGF (28 May 2026) is its TFAIA framework and EU Code summary; xAI's Dec 2025 edition claimed TFAIA compliance but the Jun 2026 edition is silent on it; no Google or Meta SB 53 document found. Anthropic RSP v3.4 remains current (page updated 14 Aug 2026 with the Aug 2026 Risk Report).

### B3 multilateral bodies and processes (L1): AISR, AISI Network/NAAIMES, AI summit series, OECD (incl. HAIP), Council of Europe, UNESCO; UN bodies as proposed additions

Since June 2026: the network issued its first best-practice guidance (Jul 2026). No new AISR publication after 3 Feb 2026. Geneva summit fixed for 21–22 Jun 2027 with Fabiola Gianotti as delegate; UAE co-chairs 2027 and hosts 2028. Delhi Declaration reached 92 endorsers. OECD AI Recommendation gained Cambodia and Croatia (May 2026). EU concluded the CoE Convention (Apr/May 2026), but it is not in force. UNESCO Global Forum (Riyadh, Sep 2026) produced no new instrument. UN Scientific Panel issued its Preliminary Report (1 Jul 2026) and a loss-of-control brief (21 Sep 2026); first Global Dialogue held Jul 2026. Drafted one addition (UN Panel & Dialogue).

### United Kingdom

No AI bill. The 13 May 2026 King's Speech dropped frontier-AI legislation; AI appears only as sandboxes in a Regulating for Growth Bill (not yet introduced). Lord Holmes's AI (Regulation) Bill [HL] (the map's link) was not carried over. A Labour backbencher introduced an Artificial Superintelligence Bill (session 2026-27).

Searches: “UK Parliament Bills API: search 'artificial intelligence', 'superintelligence', 'frontier', 'Regulating for Growth'”; “GOV.UK search API: King's Speech 2026; statutory footing AI Security Institute”; “WebSearch: King's Speech May 2026 artificial intelligence bill”

### China

No new national AI law. The CAC keeps publishing generative AI filing lists (latest attachment Aug 2026). On 3 Jul 2026 it re-consulted on a revised Internet Information Services Measures with an AI chapter. Humanlike interactive AI measures (in force Jul 2026) are already mentioned in cn-ai-law.

### South Korea

The AI Basic Act entered into force 22 Jan 2026 together with its Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 36053). The decree sets the 10^26 FLOPs safety threshold with two further criteria. A partial amendment (Act No. 21311, 20 Jan 2026) is fully in force from 21 Jul 2026 but does not touch the frontier provisions.
